title: Supreme Court Starts New Term With Big Cases to Watch
summary:
The U.S. Supreme Court returns on Monday to start a new term. A term is the yearly period when the court hears cases and makes decisions. This year, the justices will look at several big questions that affect people across the country.

One case is about climate change. The city and county of Boulder, Colorado, sued two energy companies, Suncor and Exxon Mobil, in 2018. The city and county say the companies knew they were contributing to climate change and that this harmed the area and its residents. Boulder wants money to help pay for that harm. The companies say federal law and the U.S. Constitution block these lawsuits. The court will hear arguments on October 5. Justice Samuel Alito stepped aside from this case on September 28, so he will not take part.

Another case is about guns. In December, the court will hear about a local law in Illinois. That law bans the possession, sale and transfer of assault weapons, including AR-15s. Some residents and gun rights groups sued. They say the law violates their constitutional rights. The court will decide whether the Second and 14th Amendments protect the right to own semiautomatic weapons.

The court also handles emergency requests. These are called the "shadow docket." The justices often make quick, temporary decisions without long explanations. In September, for example, the court temporarily blocked an effort by President Donald Trump to restrict mail-in voting.

More cases may be added later. The court could still take up cases about the military's ban on transgender members or Trump's appeal in a defamation case brought by writer E. Jean Carroll. Experts say the court hears fewer full cases than in the past, and more of its work now happens on the emergency docket.
why_it_matters: The Supreme Court's decisions can change rules and rights across the whole country, so it helps to know which big questions it will consider.

questions.question: What is a "term" for the Supreme Court?
options: A short break between important court cases
The yearly period when it hears cases and makes decisions
A list of laws that Congress recently passed
The group of judges who sit on the court
questions.correct_answer: The yearly period when it hears cases and makes decisions

questions.question: What is the "shadow docket"?

Emergency requests that justices often decide quickly and temporarily
A list of cases the court finished last year
